{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOUDROfM8AAAABX0rVvg", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BlR_zzhBZEbU", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BlR_z", "number": 121, "title": "Add local Parakeet v3 and Moonshine Medium Streaming ASR Nodes to the Chrome extension", "body": "## Problem

English speech-to-text quality with the current lightweight Streaming Zipformer 20M is not satisfactory in real use. We want to add two promising ASR models as **independent, opt-in processing Nodes** in the existing Chrome extension Graph Editor, so the user can test and compare them later without replacing or destabilizing existing processors.

This Issue covers **implementation, integration, and verifiable operation**, **not a subjective quality ranking or user-run comparison**. The user will evaluate transcription quality separately.

## Expected outcome

### Add two real model-specific ASR Nodes

1. **NVIDIA Parakeet TDT 0.6B v3** (e.g. `SpeechToTextParakeetV3`). Use the actual `nvidia/parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3` model or a verified browser-compatible ONNX conversion of that exact model, not another Parakeet version. Evaluate the browser `parakeet.js` / ONNX Runtime Web implementation first. Confirm the exact model/conversion revision, runtime, model license (CC BY 4.0), asset sizes, hardware requirements and inference correctness before choosing and pinning them.
2. **Moonshine Voice English Medium Streaming** (e.g. `SpeechToTextMoonshineMediumEn`). Use the **245M English Medium Streaming** model and its supported JavaScript/WASM runtime (investigate official `@moonshine-ai/moonshine-wasm`), not Moonshine tiny, small or older nonstreaming models. Confirm the exact checkpoint/runtime revision, license (currently documented MIT), assets, browser compatibility and actual streaming behavior before pinning them.

Both are independent concrete processor Nodes, not a global model selector, new ASR SDK, generic model registry or replacement of existing ReazonSpeech, Whisper tiny, or Zipformer Nodes.

### Graph contracts and behavior

- Consume the existing `audio: MONO_16KHZ_PCM` from Chrome tab, microphone or selected-media source, using the existing local capture/resampler helpers. Do not alter the shared capture/PCM Port contract.
- Emit **`final: TEXT`** with real committed recognized text. Expose **`provisional: TEXT` only if that exact model/runtime truly supports useful interim recognition**; do not synthesize fake previews by replaying finals or advertise a port that never emits. Moonshine Medium Streaming is expected to support genuinely incremental output; investigate Parakeet v3's live/chunked facilities and document its actual behavior. Keep ports minimal and model-faithful.
- Integrate both independently in `NODE_TYPES`, the searchable Add Node palette, graph validation, session builder, multi-ASR resource ownership, Live output and existing fan-out to TextFormatter / OPUS-MT / focused text fields. Any processor can be selected and wired separately; both may appear in one graph and run on separate paths when resources permit.
- Preserve complete/final utterance ordering and avoid duplicates, lost tails, stale partials and cross-session output. Specify model-appropriate endpointing/chunk policies, bounded input/backlog and any expected segmentation quality/latency compromises. Support model readiness, Stop/drain, Cancel, repeated Start, errors and release of Workers/GPU/WASM/media resources.
- Inference must execute **locally inside the Chrome extension**, with no speech upload, remote inference API or recording-time executable/runtime downloads. Comply with Manifest V3 CSP. Document and report GPU support/failure clearly; use an actually tested fallback **only if practical**, rather than inventing a fallback or silently falling back to another ASR model.

### Model setup and usability

- Follow the project's existing graph-driven **Save → prepare required model assets** flow for optional weights. Reuse pinned checksum-verified download/cache machinery (and progress/retry/cancellation) where practical; do not silently bundle multi-GB weights into the default extension or automatically download unused models. A saved but disconnected/inactive ASR Node may remain parked; preparation should follow the current saved-node model preparation policy.
- Pin exact compatible model conversion/runtime artifacts and record hashes, size, origin and license/attribution. No dynamic remote JavaScript. Clearly state expected download/storage and GPU/CPU memory needs before a large model download, with actionable error/retry behavior; a failed download must not destroy the saved graph.
- Keep the default graph and all existing version 9 saved graphs and prior migrations unchanged. Do not add new graph-level cardinality restrictions, modify the existing translation workflow or expand the generic Pipeline without a concrete need.

### Testing, documentation, and scope

- Add deterministic Node, graph, error/lifecycle, resource and model-preparation tests for both processors.
- **Run real pinned-model inference** for **each** model using the production extension graph/Worker/backend under the packaged MV3 environment and reproducible English speech fixtures. Verify meaningful final TEXT (and actual pre-final provisional events if exposed), repeat/Stop/Cancel and no inference-network requests. A fake Worker/fixture alone is insufficient.
- Include a focused native tab-capture or microphone-to-Node integration check where practical, and document any hardware-dependent skips accurately.
- Record observations for startup/first text/final latency, asset footprint and CPU/GPU/memory where feasible, with test hardware and limitations. **Do not claim improvement over Zipformer based solely on successful inference or a few fixtures.** Real meeting-room accuracy, comparative WER/CER, subjective language quality and user acceptance are **out of scope** for this implementation Issue.
- Update README, Node/Port graph docs, extension setup/model documentation, provenance/terms and optional real-model test instructions.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] Both actual, named models load and perform local inference in a packaged Chrome MV3 extension with pinned, license-reviewed assets. Both new Node types appear in the Graph Editor and can be saved, reloaded, and used in otherwise independent paths without changing existing defaults.
- [ ] Existing audio sources connect to each new Node via `MONO_16KHZ_PCM`; its committed `final: TEXT` connects to `LiveTextDisplay.append`, optional translators and TextFormatter. Interim output ports appear only when real interim results can be demonstrated.
- [ ] Real-model, model-specific English speech fixtures produce useful, nonempty final text for each processor; if provisional is supported, real inference demonstrates changing provisional before the corresponding final. Test evidence distinguishes fixture recognition from real-world accuracy.
- [ ] Stop drains recognized tails, Cancel releases work, repeated starts do not leak stale outputs, and failure/missing GPU/model assets produce actionable errors without breaking unrelated paths. Exercise concurrent graph compatibility with appropriately bounded resources.
- [ ] Exact revisions/checksums, weight preparation, cache reuse, progress/retry, offline inference, MV3 CSP compliance, permissions, licensing and model-size/memory limits are validated and documented.
- [ ] Relevant unit, browser and packaged-extension integration tests/build pass; report skips, device limitations and measured performance honestly. Existing models/default graph and saved Graph v9 behaviors regressions pass.

## Required post-merge verification

None. Any check that can be performed only after merge must be recorded separately as pending if discovered; it must not block pre-merge acceptance.

## Context

- Existing ASR Node integration: `extension/graph.js`, `extension/graph-runtime.js`, `extension/session.js`, `web/zipformer-node.js`, `web/whisper-node.js`.
- Setup and verified assets: `extension/graph-page.js`, Graph Editor model preparation, `extension/model-asset-cache.js`, `scripts/`, `docs/zipformer-node.md`.
- Product direction: #7. Independent graph paths and saved drafts: #115. Graph-driven model preparation: #117.
- Official model: https://huggingface.co/nvidia/parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3
- Browser implementation to evaluate: https://github.com/ysdede/parakeet.js
- Moonshine models: https://moonshine-voice.readthedocs.io/en/latest/models/available-models/
- Moonshine JS/WASM quickstart: https://moonshine-voice.readthedocs.io/en/latest/quickstart/
